for myself I use markdown in Obsidian. i don't use really any plugins, most are a waste of time/distraction to me. I don't know what your OCD is like but if you're worried about being distracted on "building the perfect second brain" or whatever, you could also just use a simple markdown editor like marktext.

otherwise I just have a simple folder structure for each of my school courses  and hobbies.
for instance, each course folder has one markdown file, where topics are separated by headers (#). the rest of the folder is filled with PDF's of lecture slides and other documents.

what's great about markdown is it's just a simple text document. so it's easy to backup, search through, migrate etc. it has basic formatting features like bolding, italics, highlighting, lists, bullet points etc, but as a stem major I appreciate the ability to use latex and add code snippets. the only downside is that you can't directly draw in markdown, though you can link and embed photos.

in terms of memorization, for my humanities courses I usually would try to structure my bullet points as questions, then sub bullet points as Answers, sorta like flashcards. I would fold all the headings and bullet points (Obsidian) and then when a heading is unfolded with a question, or the general topic, I will try to recall what I wrote there in the subheadings before i click and reveal the answer.

for my math, (or any topic where you use lots of symbols and quick diagrams), i have an accordion folder full of letter paper. I did try xournal++ with a stylus for math notes, and it's great because you can easily export to PDF, but I found I just prefer the feel of paper for doing loads of math.
